$comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): a C99 6.7.4p7 inline definition that is CALLED but whose external definition exists in no linked TU must fail LOUD at the link tier, naming the symbol. The negative half of `inline_c99_inline_definition_crosscu` -- same source shape, sibling CU removed. ★ 'Emits nothing' is only a safe decision if the omission is DETECTABLE: encoding the state as a weak binding, or as a silently dropped declaration, would turn this program into a wrong-body call or a mysterious crash instead of a diagnostic. Fail-loud here is the contract that makes the no-emit decision safe everywhere else, and it is the same contract a bare prototype with no definition already has. MEASURED: `/usr/bin/clang -std=c99 -O0` on this exact file also fails to link, with `Undefined symbols: _missing_body`. ★★★ AND AT RELEASE THIS EXACT PROGRAM NOW LINKS AND RUNS (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-NO-EXTERNAL-DEFINITION-EMITTED, 2026-08-15) -- which is not a contradiction of the pin above but the OTHER half of 6.7.4p7: the inline definition is 'an alternative to an external definition, which a translator may use to implement any call to the function in the same translation unit', so once the inliner takes the call there is no reference left to be undefined. ✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 / clang 18.1.3 / clang 19 all behave identically on this shape: link failure at -O0, success at -O1 and above. ⚠ THIS EXAMPLE THEREFORE DECLARES NO OPTIMIZED ARM, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT -- the runner requires an example's BASELINE arm to build and run before it will compare an optimized one, so a shape whose two arms differ in KIND (diagnostic vs running binary) cannot be expressed here at all. The release half is witnessed instead by inline_c99_inline_definition_crosscu, whose release arm exits 7 because the inline definition was used, and by the sqlite hwtime.h construct measured through the CLI.
